claims.text: The starting refractory high-entropy alloy has a coarse-grained homogenized microstructure with minimal secondary-phase precipitates.
Adding approximately 1–3 at% Zr and applying controlled aging will induce nanoprecipitate formation.
The intervention will produce a fine dispersion of coherent Zr-rich nanoprecipitates.
Diffusion-driven precipitation during aging can occur while the alloy retains a stable primary refractory phase such as BCC.
Optimized aging can maintain fine, coherent nanoprecipitates without excessive coarsening.
The coherent Zr-rich nanoprecipitates obstruct dislocation motion.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by the nanoprecipitates increases yield strength.
The nanoprecipitates serve as sites that promote beneficial deformation mechanisms.
The proposed precipitate-mediated deformation behavior improves plasticity.
The Zr-modified and aged alloy will have higher yield strength than an alloy lacking both the Zr addition and tailored aging.
The Zr-modified and aged alloy will have greater elongation to failure than an alloy lacking both the Zr addition and tailored aging.
Heat-treatment temperatures, times, or compositions that inhibit formation of fine coherent precipitates may prevent the predicted strength and ductility improvements.
